rationale: The paper develops an optimization algorithm (hybrid ANLS with modified nonmonotone line search) to fit nonnegative matrix factorization on synthetic and real datasets, which is an unsupervised matrix-factorization/dimensionality-reduction method. The subject is optimization and numerical analysis, hence the Mathematics/Applied mathematics domain tags.

The paper is a magnetohydrodynamics/fluid-mechanics study (physics) where bvp4c numerical solutions are used as training data for an artificial neural network, i.e. supervised fitting of an ANN trained in this study. The abstract gives no depth indication for the ANN, so the family is 'classic neural network'; bvp4c itself is a numerical solver, not an ML model.

The paper's only ML method is K-means cluster analysis, trained on CEPS questionnaire data to identify parent-child interaction and school adaptation patterns; the ANOVA and correlation analyses are statistical tests, not predictive models. The subject is adolescent mental health, best captured by Medicine > Psychiatry.

A clinical risk prediction nomogram for unmet psychological care needs in hepatocellular carcinoma was built with LASSO feature selection and multivariable logistic regression on retrospective patient data, i.e. supervised classical ML models trained in this study. The subject spans psychiatric/psychological care needs in an oncology (HCC) population; no tier3 term fits the prediction-model focus.

The paper fits a multivariable binary logistic regression prediction model on retrospective patient data with internal validation (cross-validation, bootstrap), a supervised training task. The subject is cardiology (STEMI/PCI/heart failure) in a diabetic population, so Medicine with Cardiology and Endocrinology and metabolism domains apply.

The paper trains a LASSO-Cox regression model on multicenter perioperative data to build a prognostic nomogram for overall survival, externally validated in an independent cohort. This is supervised classical statistical learning for survival prediction in oncology; no deep learning, LLM, or other model family is named.

The paper trains a YOLOv8n object-detection model on 3255 annotated crack images for supervised crack detection, so the model is trained in this study with a supervised paradigm and a deep-learning family. The subject is vision-based robotics/computer vision for structural inspection, best captured by Computer science with Imaging and Machine learning; no tier3 term fits crack detection, and robotics itself is not in the vocabulary.

ChatGPT-4 was used with chain-of-thought prompting to predict therapeutic targets of 6M1@C60, with no model training or fine-tuning reported. The paper's biomedical focus is fullerene biomaterials for atherosclerosis (cardiovascular disease) with mechanistic validation of the NRF2/HO-1/GPX4 ferroptosis axis.

The paper trains four supervised classifiers (LR, RF, SVM, XGBoost) on retrospective patient data for sepsis and mortality prediction, with nomograms derived from the best models; SHAP is interpretation-only and excluded. Domain centers on biliary disease (cholangitis) with sepsis, using machine learning methods.

The paper trains age-specific logistic regression models on questionnaire item data to differentially diagnose depressive disorder vs. insomnia disorder, a supervised classification task using classical machine learning. The subject is clinical psychiatry (differential diagnosis of depression and insomnia), with no tier3 domain term applicable.

A purely methodological ML paper that trains its own fair models via invariant representation learning to preserve fairness and accuracy under domain shift; no specific architecture or algorithm name beyond invariant representation learning is given, and the domain is computer science/machine learning rather than a biomedical field.

The paper trains a hybrid deep learning model (BiLSTM + Transformer + temporal CNN) for photovoltaic power prediction and fault diagnosis, a supervised task evaluated with accuracy metrics. No EDAM biomedical domain applies, and the Golden Jackal/grey wolf optimizers are hyperparameter tuning methods for the neural models rather than the paper's own learning methods.

The paper develops an R bioinformatics workflow for BALF metagenomic (microbial) and host transcriptomic analysis, fitting a nearest-centroid host-transcriptome model and logistic regression microbial models (supervised, classical ML) for lung cancer vs infection classification. Domain terms reflect metagenomic sequencing/analysis rather than clinical practice.

The paper's domain is fluorescence imaging and analysis of primary cilia (cell biology), with Cilia SubQ built around the newly developed Cilia.AI deep learning segmentation model. Since Cilia.AI is a newly developed model recognizing cilia with minimal manual correction, it is trained in this study in a supervised manner.

No biomedical domain applies, so the subject is tagged as Computer science with Machine learning.

Multi-omics (proteomic and lipidomic) study of lipid-protein oxidation in air-dried hairtail, with seven ML models fitted to identify oxidative biomarkers; XGBoost is the only named model and performed best (AUC 0.98). Training is supervised classification on the paper's own omics data.

The paper trains a multimodal supervised classifier for lung adenocarcinoma subtyping, combining radiomic and deep-learning (ResNet-101) features with classical ML models. Lasso and logistic regression, plus SVM/SMOTE and XGBoost fusion, are the named model types; SHAP/ICE and feature-selection steps (Boruta, RFE) are explainability/selection methods, not model types.

The paper's only machine-learning method is k-means clustering of coping profiles (unsupervised, fit on the study's own data); the multiple regression and bootstrap mediation analyses are association-testing statistics, not predictive models, so they are excluded per the model_type rules. The subject domain is chronic spinal pain assessment within medicine.

The paper trains penalized logistic regression variants (ridge, lasso, elastic net) with cross-validated tuning on the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset for supervised classification. No deep, generative, or other model families are involved; the domain is biomedical ML applied to breast cancer diagnosis.

The paper trains SSFDD, a semi-supervised one-stage anchor-based detector combining RetinaNet's architecture with YOLOv5's anchor design and teacher-student pseudo-labelling, so it is trained in this study with a semi-supervised paradigm. Domain is an AI/computer-vision method applied to aquaculture fish disease, with no further tier3 vocabulary fit.

The paper trains a 3D diffusion autoencoder on cardiac MRI to derive latent phenotypes without labels, so it is a deep, representation-learning model trained in an unsupervised manner. The domains reflect the cardiology imaging focus, the ML methodology, and the downstream GWAS linking derived traits to genetic variants.

The paper's subject is head and neck oncology treatment pathways, studied via a bibliometric text-mining analysis. It fits an unsupervised five-topic LDA topic model on the literature corpus and an exploratory supervised logistic life-cycle model; bibliometric methods like co-citation and keyword analysis are not ML models.

The study applies the pretrained SpliceAI deep learning tool to predict splice-altering variants, validated experimentally with minigene assays; no model is trained in this paper. Domains reflect the genetic-variant interpretation focus in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

The paper trains a LASSO model on GEO osteoarthritis transcriptomic data to identify MPO as a key gene, alongside unsupervised clustering and single-cell bioinformatics analysis; molecular docking and dynamics simulation are physics/chemistry methods, not ML model types. The subject is an osteoarthritis mechanism study combining bioinformatics with rat-model and in-vitro validation of resveratrol.

This is a medical (occupational health/burnout) intervention study in military OB/GYN physicians; the only modelling is a latent profile analysis fit to Maslach Burnout Inventory scores, an unsupervised classical ML method used to identify burnout profiles. No supervised training, deep learning, or pretrained models are mentioned.

The paper is a stroke-focused integrative study combining Mendelian randomization with downstream bioinformatics and a machine-learning feature-selection step, but it names no specific ML algorithm (SHAP and molecular docking are excluded by the model-type rules), so model_type and model_family stay empty while supervised training is implied. Domains center on neurology/stroke with genetic (GWAS/MR) evidence.

The study trains elastic net, random forest and gradient boosting regressors with cross-validation to predict psychotropic medication adherence, an all-classical supervised learning setup with ensembles; SHAP is explainability and is excluded from model types. Domains center on psychiatry/patient adherence prediction using machine learning.

The study applies a vendor-supplied deep learning MRI reconstruction algorithm based on convolutional neural networks to brain DWI data without training, so the model is pretrained and applied as-is with no learning paradigm. The subject is clinical MRI imaging of intracranial tumors, hence the medicine/imaging/oncology domains.

The paper trains multiple ML classifiers on a newly created DDoS network-flow dataset (MedibotDDoS), with random forest as the only named and best-performing algorithm; other algorithms are unnamed so cannot be tagged. The subject is cybersecurity/ML applied to medical IoT, fitting Informatics with Medical informatics and Machine learning domains; no tier3 term applies.

The paper trains biologically informed neural networks (BINNs) and the LEMBAS recurrent neural network framework on signaling data, a supervised predictive task with L2 regularization. It is a computational/systems-biology methods paper published in Bioinformatics, modeling intracellular signaling networks.

The paper trains supervised defect-classification models on sensor signals and proposes LARM, a data augmentation technique (excluded as a training technique, not a model type). No specific model architecture or algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family are left empty; the subject is an ML method for manufacturing quality monitoring, best captured as computer science / machine learning.

The paper is a bacterial RNA-seq transcriptomics study of avian pathogenic E. coli during embryo infection; its computational analyses (differential expression, enrichment, small RNA profiling, WGCNA) are bioinformatics pipeline/network methods rather than named ML models, so no model fields apply. Domains reflect microbiology, systems biology, and transcriptomics.

The paper trains three nnU-Net v2 segmentation models on CT data to quantify lobar and airway volumes, a supervised deep learning task in the medical imaging domain. No pretrained, prompted, or additional model types are described, so a single deep-learning segmentation model is tagged.

The paper trains a deep-learning echocardiographic model on expert TTE data with confirmed HCM labels, a supervised task, and validates it on POCUS studies; no specific architecture or algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type is left empty and the family is deep learning. Domains reflect cardiology screening via echocardiographic imaging.

The paper fine-tunes self-supervised speech foundation models (WavLM, HuBERT) on a labelled MDD vs control cohort for diagnostic classification, with pretrained models also compared as-is against conventional openSMILE acoustic features. Domains center on psychiatric diagnosis via speech biomarkers using machine learning.

The paper trains a deep-learning CT radiomics model and a multi-instance-learning pathomics model (weak/multiple-instance supervision) alongside a clinical model, then fuses them via late-fusion logistic regression, so semi-supervised is added alongside supervised. Domains center on oncological prognosis prediction using imaging and pathology, i.e., Medicine > Oncology/Imaging > Medical imaging.

The paper trains its own RT-DETR-based detection transformer (DSCF-DET) with custom modules on a labelled wildlife image dataset for fine-grained species detection, i.e. supervised training of a deep learning model. The subject is ecological wildlife monitoring of musk deer, so Biology/Ecology/Biodiversity domains apply.

The study integrates single-cell eQTL/GWAS Mendelian randomization, WGCNA, differential expression, docking and simulation to prioritize HNC targets, and trains a dual-gene diagnostic model (AUC 0.917), but no specific ML algorithm or model family is named in the abstract. Mendelian randomization, WGCNA, docking and molecular dynamics are excluded per the model-type rules, so only the supervised training of the unnamed diagnostic model is recorded.

The paper trains nine supervised ML models on survey data to predict presenteeism, selecting predictors with LASSO and multiple linear regression and finding the generalized additive model optimal; SHAP and network analysis are interpretation/analysis methods, not model types. No deep, generative, or unsupervised learning step is involved.

Elastic net regressions were fitted in the lifestyle validation studies to build the multimetabolite scores, a supervised model-fitting use, so elastic net is tagged as the trained model; the Cox/hazard-ratio analyses are association testing and are excluded. The paper's subject is diet quality and coronary heart disease risk in large prospective cohorts, with metabolomics serving as an intermediate marker rather than the primary domain.

A radiomics-based machine learning model was trained on preoperative CECT features to predict recurrence-free survival in GIST patients, a supervised survival-prediction task in oncology imaging. The abstract names no specific algorithm, so model_type and model_family are left empty per the evidence rules.

This is a psychometric validation study of a translated GAD-7 anxiety scale; its analytical models are exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses fit on survey data. EFA is an unsupervised latent-variable/dimensionality-reduction method, and no named AI/ML algorithm beyond these appears in the abstract.

The study trains five ML algorithms (LASSO, random forest, Boruta, gradient boosting machine, XGBoost) on transcriptomic data to identify UC biomarker genes, i.e. supervised feature-selection/classification models, mostly ensemble tree methods plus LASSO. Domain is inflammatory bowel disease research combining bulk and single-cell RNA-seq; WGCNA, pseudotime and cell-cell communication analyses are bioinformatics pipeline methods, not model types.

The paper trains ensemble models (gradient boosting, random forest) as core supervised predictors of CD4 outcomes, with LSTM and Transformer deep networks as comparative benchmarks on longitudinal data. The domain is HIV treatment optimization via digital twins, a personalised-medicine/medical-informatics application of infectious disease management.

The paper fits a logistic regression model combining three cytokines to discriminate clinical stage transition in first-episode psychosis (AUC 0.853), a supervised classical ML model trained in this study. The subject is psychiatric biomarker research (plasma immune profiles in psychosis), with no deeper domain terms applicable.

The paper trains a multi-pose shared-encoder Vision Transformer on standardised pre-operative facial photographs to predict difficult tracheal intubation, a supervised classification task in anaesthesiology using facial image data; no other AI models or training paradigms are named.

The paper develops and trains HPNet, a supervised deep CNN built on a RepVGG-D2se backbone, for head pose estimation to quantify cervical range of motion. The domain is clinical measurement of neck movement via camera imaging, with musculoskeletal relevance.

The paper mines prescription drug-class combinations in Medicare claims using frequent itemset mining (an unsupervised association-rule method) applied to its own cohort data, alongside regression models used only to estimate adjusted rate ratios. The subject is pharmacoepidemiology of polypharmacy in incident epilepsy, hence Medicine with Neurology and Public health and epidemiology; no tier3 term fits better than the general pharmacoepidemiologic framing.

This is a parasitic-infection immunology study of the hepatic alveolar echinococcosis immune microenvironment using imaging mass cytometry. The only ML components are unsupervised analyses applied to the paper's own single-cell data: PhenoGraph clustering and t-SNE dimensionality reduction.

The paper trains a supervised logistic regression classifier on non-targeted LC-MS chemical fingerprints of honey to predict botanical origin, applying it across instruments after a spectral-transformation step; the domain is analytical chemistry/metabolomics of small-molecule food authentication.

The paper trains variational autoencoders to embed longitudinal item data into a shared latent space (unsupervised), then applies a mixed-effects regression on the latent representations; the application is quantifying treatment-switch effects in spinal muscular atrophy, a paediatric rare neuromuscular disease.

The paper trains an improved YOLO26n-seg-SAConv model from scratch (architecture modification with SAConv) on labelled DR images for Genant classification of vertebral compression fractures, a supervised deep learning task. The domain is medical imaging analysis for a musculoskeletal condition, so Imaging/Machine learning and Medical imaging are the most central tags.

The study develops a polygenic risk score (PRS-KLK3int) fit on discovery data and validated in independent sets, a weighted SNP-based predictive model trained on labelled aggressiveness outcomes (supervised), with no named ML algorithm beyond the PRS itself. The subject domain is genetic risk prediction of prostate cancer aggressiveness.

This is a pure machine-learning methods paper proposing ADIMC, an unsupervised incremental multi-view clustering framework trained from scratch on benchmark datasets, with no biomedical application domain stated. The anchor-graph construction and disentanglement components are non-neural, so they map to classical machine learning plus representation learning.

The paper trains a DeepSurv deep neural network on HCC patient data to build a prognostic risk model, so model_use is trained-in-study with supervised learning and deep learning as the family. The subject is multi-omics (eQTL, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics) applied to hepatocellular carcinoma tumor microenvironment and prognosis.

The paper trains 1D and 2D convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet, GoogLeNet, DenseNet, AlexNet) from scratch on ultrasonic Rayleigh wave signals and power spectrum images to classify four roller damage types, a supervised deep learning task in ultrasonic non-destructive testing (physics/engineering domain).

The paper trains a graph isomorphism network (a GNN) from scratch on protein-ligand complexes for binding affinity prediction with an auxiliary IC50 multi-task branch, i.e. a supervised deep learning model trained in this study. The subject is computational modeling of protein-ligand interactions for drug discovery/cheminformatics.

The paper trains two CNN models (UC-Re for binary remission classification, UC-MES for four-class Mayo Endoscopic Score grading) on labelled endoscopy images, i.e. supervised deep learning. Domain is gastroenterology/endoscopy imaging; inpainting and image harmonization are preprocessing techniques, not model types.

The paper builds reservoir-computing networks (fixed random-weight RNNs) whose trained readout layer is fitted to tasks, i.e. models trained in this study via supervised learning on the readout. The reservoir is a non-deep recurrent architecture, so 'classic neural network' is the appropriate family rather than deep learning; the study is computational neuroscience of network dynamics (Neurobiology, Machine learning).

DeepKOALA is a GRU-based deep learning model trained in this study for supervised KEGG Orthology assignment, framed as open-set recognition. The domain is computational sequence annotation, spanning bioinformatics, sequence analysis and functional genomics.

The paper fits a Bayesian network model to cross-sectional survey data to reveal psychological pathways linking pregnancy app engagement to health literacy, so the model is trained in this study via unsupervised structure learning within the classical machine learning family. The subject is a maternal digital health survey, best captured as Medicine with Public health and epidemiology and Medical informatics as tier-2 domains.

The paper's 'combined model' is a biomarker panel evaluated with ROC curves, generalized estimating equations, correlation, and bootstrap mediation analyses — statistical/diagnostic methods, none of which constitutes a named machine-learning algorithm, so no model types or families are tagged. The subject domain is early diagnosis of pancreatic encephalopathy in severe acute pancreatitis, spanning gastroenterology and neurology in a clinical cohort study.

The paper trains thirteen machine-learning and deep-learning models on SERS spectra of vaginal fluid for four-class diagnosis, with the one-dimensional convolutional neural network performing best, indicating supervised training. Only the 1DCNN is named among the evaluated models, and majority-vote classification implies an ensemble voting step.

The paper trains a hybrid graph attention autoencoder (GAT-AE) on a CLASH-derived bipartite sRNA-mRNA interaction graph, reconstructing edge-weight interaction scores, so the model is trained in-study in a supervised (regression) manner using deep learning (graph attention layers plus an autoencoder with feedforward decoder). The domain is computational modeling of posttranscriptional sRNA regulation in S. aureus in the context of peri-implantitis.

The study trains classical statistical models (logistic regression, class weighting, SMOTE-resampled and Elastic Net variants) on Colombian surveillance data to predict severe low birth weight, a supervised classification task; SMOTE and class weighting are training/resampling techniques rather than model types, so only the two named model types are tagged. The subject is neonatal/public-health epidemiology, hence Medicine with Public health and epidemiology and Paediatrics.

The study applies single-cell RNA-seq with unsupervised clustering, cell-cell interaction analysis, and enrichment analyses to profile age-related endothelial changes, fitting an Omics/transcriptomics domain. No specific ML algorithm or model family is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family remain empty despite the unsupervised clustering learning step.

The study develops Vision Transformer Base/16-based nomograms from serial ultrasound images for graft-outcome prediction, with a pretrained ViT adapted to the transplant imaging data in a supervised manner alongside a radiomics nomogram comparator; imaging domains reflect the ultrasound/radiomics focus in post-transplant medicine.

The study trains separate 2x2 self-organizing maps (unsupervised) on Delphi consensus data stratified by expert profile to select palliative care integration indicators. The subject is health services research on palliative care in primary care, best captured as Medicine with Public health and epidemiology.

A CT/CTA radiomics model was trained with LASSO feature selection and eleven classifiers to predict complete recanalization after thrombectomy, with logistic regression selected as the final supervised classifier. The eleven competing classifiers are not individually named, so only LASSO and logistic regression can be tagged as model types.

The paper fits latent profile analysis to questionnaire data to identify attachment subgroups (unsupervised learning), while ANOVA/ANCOVA, chi-square tests and adjusted logistic regression serve only as statistical association analyses, not predictive ML models. The subject is nursing-student mental health and workforce retention, best captured under Medicine with Psychiatry and Public health and epidemiology.

A supervised mortality-prediction model was trained on MIMIC-IV/eICU-CRD data, with LASSO and Boruta for feature screening and six ML models compared, of which random forest was the named best performer. Logistic regression and RCS were used for association testing rather than as the predictive model, and SHAP is explainability only.

The paper trains a stacked ensemble model on a nationwide Japanese HSCT registry cohort to predict cGVHD, NRM and ACM, with Cox-PH, Random Survival Forest, XGBoost and Dynamic-DeepHit as base/weaker learners, so supervised training with stacking (ensemble learning) plus classical ML and deep learning families applies. Domain-wise the work centres on haematological malignancy transplantation and GVHD immunology in a clinical cohort.

The paper trains binary logistic regression diagnostic models on serum tumor marker data from a retrospective lung cancer cohort, a supervised classical ML approach. The subject is oncology diagnostics using biomarker panels, with no higher-tier3 domain term clearly warranted.

The paper engineers dome-level image features and trains a TabNet deep tabular model to classify qPCR-defined cytokine responsiveness, a supervised task on its own data. Domain terms reflect the imaging-guided organoid/inflammation application of machine learning.

The paper trains a shared encoder-decoder network for event-based optical flow using a label-free radial consistency loss (self-supervised pre-training) followed by optional supervised fine-tuning on small labeled sets. E-RAFT and EV-FlowNet are only comparators, and no domain biology/medicine applies beyond computer vision and machine learning.

The paper trains five CNN classifiers (EfficientNet best) on processed pediatric occlusal radiographs for supervised classification, with a fuzzy control strategy ensemble (majority voting, weighted confidence) integrating their outputs. The domain is dental/medical imaging AI, best captured by Medicine > Dentistry/Imaging > Medical imaging.

The paper fits a Kuenm-optimized MaxEnt (maximum entropy) species distribution model to field occurrence data to project ragweed habitat under climate scenarios, which is a supervised classical ML model trained in this study. The subject domain is ecology/biodiversity (invasive species distribution under climate change), with no other model architectures named.

The paper fits a supervised prediction model for difficult facemask ventilation using facial shape features from 3D scans, but the abstract names no specific ML algorithm or architecture (the 'established facial model' is applied only to extract shape coefficients), so model_type and model_family are left empty. The subject is anaesthesiology airway assessment using 3D face imaging for digital phenotyping.

The paper develops an SPRM platform for multiparametric single-cell biophysical phenotyping, including a parasite model (Entamoeba histolytica), so Biophysics and Phenomics are the most central domains. The abstract states only that 'machine learning' classified early single-cell phenotypes against reference groups, with no algorithm or family named, so model_type/model_family remain empty while supervised training is implied by the classification task.

The paper trains a multimodal machine-learning framework on ADNI data to predict cerebral microhemorrhage outcomes (supervised learning), integrating imaging, biomarkers, and clinical history. The abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type is empty and model_family is tagged only as multimodal learning.

The paper trains autoencoders and unsupervised clustering on fused histology/RNA-seq features, while a pretrained ResNet-50 is applied as-is for tile embedding. All learning steps are unsupervised; Cox and log-rank analyses are association statistics, not predictive models.

The paper performs whole-genome sequencing-based rare variant discovery in JIA families, so the domains are genetics/genomics with WGS and variant-phenotype terms. The only AI method is AlphaFold structure modeling used as an off-the-shelf tool to predict variant effects, hence pretrained as-is with no training in this study.

The paper trains regression models on metabolite and transcriptomic data to predict post-season levels and cross-platform molecular information (supervised prediction), but names no specific algorithm, so a generic regression model under classical machine learning is tagged. Domains reflect the neuroscience/TBI focus with metabolomic, transcriptomic, and epigenetic analyses.

The paper trains a reinforcement learning agent (on error-detection events from quantum error correction) to steer control parameters of a superconducting quantum processor; the subject is quantum computing/physics, and the agent's architecture is not named, so no model_family term applies.

A prognostic prediction model for time-structured 30-day readmission risk was developed on the paper's own cohorts (supervised learning), but the abstract names no algorithm, architecture, or tool, so model_type and model_family stay empty. Domains reflect hospital readmission risk modeling for postdischarge care allocation.

The paper trains a hybrid SE-ResNet50 convolutional architecture for supervised classification of cotton leaf disease images, so the domain is plant/agricultural science with deep learning as the model family. Grad-CAM (explainability) and optimization/loss components (Weighted CrossEntropyLoss, Adam, ReduceLROnPlateau, Early Stopping) are excluded as training techniques, leaving the ResNet50 backbone and the proposed SE-ResNet50 hybrid as the model types.

The paper trains a two-stream heterogeneous graph neural network (with a graph attention stream and a Transformer stream) for supervised multi-omics disease classification, so the model is trained in-study, supervised, and belongs to deep learning; the uncertainty-aware ensemble adds the ensemble learning family. SHAP is an explainability method and FastMI is an edge-construction step, so neither is tagged as a model type.

The paper applies the pretrained Mol2Vec embedding as-is and introduces MSI, a covariance-aware Mahalanobis distance/angle similarity index over the embeddings, training no new model. Its subject is chemical-space similarity quantification for drug discovery, hence chemistry/cheminformatics domains.

The study applies two existing commercial AI segmentation tools (Blue Sky Plan and Planmeca Romexis) to cone-beam CT images of impacted mandibular third molars without any training or fine-tuning, comparing their output against manual and thresholding segmentation. Since the abstract names no algorithms or architectures behind these tools, model_family is left empty and the tools are tagged verbatim; interactive thresholding is a classical image-processing step rather than a trained ML model.

A CVD risk prediction model was trained on MESA cohort data with labelled 10-year outcomes, using logistic regression, four traditional ML algorithms and H2O AutoML, with Boruta/random-forest-based predictor selection (SHAP used only for interpretation, hence excluded). Domain is clinical cardiology risk prediction with a machine learning methodological focus.

The paper derives its CRLM risk-stratification model by projecting an epithelial cell-fate signature onto TCGA data and applying consensus clustering to define three unsupervised subtypes, so the only named model is trained in-study via unsupervised clustering. Domains reflect the multi-omics colorectal cancer liver metastasis study (scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, mutations).

The paper trains KASSPer, a supervised predictor of kinase active-site conformational states built on protein and compound language models (transformer-based, deep learning), applied to ligand-specific conformer selection for structure-based virtual screening in a drug-discovery/cheminformatics setting.

The paper fine-tunes a COCO-pretrained Mask R-CNN with ResNet50 backbone and FPN on manually annotated arthroscopy images for supervised segmentation, and also trains a U-Net (ResNet34 encoder) as a baseline comparator. The domain is orthopaedic/arthroscopic imaging applied to a musculoskeletal structure.

The study queries unnamed AI-based literature-search platforms via prompting strategies without training, fine-tuning, or naming any specific algorithm, so model_type/model_family remain empty. Domains centre on allergy/respirology evidence synthesis and AI-supported literature searching (medical informatics).

The paper trains a deep-learning semantic segmentation model on annotated oral cancer whole-slide images (supervised, from scratch), with a superpixel-based annotation/refinement workflow and QuPath deployment; since no specific architecture is named in the abstract, model_type is left empty while the family is deep learning. The domain is the medical application (oncology pathology imaging) supported by medical informatics.

The paper trains univariate/multivariate logistic regression models with LASSO variable selection on retrospective pediatric clinical data to build a differential-diagnosis nomogram for EBV-HLH vs MAS. The subject is pediatric hematology/immunology differential diagnosis; ROC/calibration/DCA are evaluations, not model types.

Organism-specific multilayer perceptron models were trained on public MIC data to predict antibacterial activity, an application of ML in antimicrobial drug discovery (cheminformatics/medicinal chemistry for veterinary pathogens). The abstract does not describe the MLP as deep, so it maps to classic neural network; calibration and applicability-domain analysis are decision/post-processing steps, not additional model types.

The paper trains a self-supervised deep reconstruction framework (TelReg and PiPM networks with multi-scale Swin Transformers) directly on undersampled k-space data, with physics constraints from the Bloch equations, so learning_paradigm is self-supervised and family is deep learning plus physics-informed ML. Domains centre on quantitative MRI for liver cancer radiotherapy (Medical imaging, MRI).

This is an integrative transcriptomics study of gastric cancer using scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq bioinformatics analyses (clustering, cell communication, pseudotime, cell death scoring, survival and drug sensitivity analyses), with no named machine learning model trained, fine-tuned, or applied. Therefore no modelling fields are tagged.

The study fits Latent Profile Analysis (a latent class/person-centered clustering model) on survey data to identify health anxiety subgroups, with BCH-based distal outcome comparison and mediation as downstream statistical analyses. The mediation and PMT constructs are standard statistical modelling rather than additional ML models, so only LPA is tagged.

A supervised transformer-based fusion model integrating radiomics, DenseNet-101 deep features and clinical variables was trained to classify tumor deposits in rectal cancer MRI. The subject is oncologic medical imaging, and only the transformer and DenseNet-101 architectures are named as trained models (the traditional DNN is a comparator).

The paper fine-tunes a pretrained foundation-model encoder with LoRA and trains the DGCL framework under webly (noisy-label, weak) supervision using a noise-aware supervised contrastive loss, which is deep-learning-based representation learning. No specific model architecture (e.g. transformer) is named in the abstract, so the model is tagged verbatim as a foundation model.

The paper trains machine learning algorithms on electrochemical sensor data for pesticide classification and concentration prediction, which is supervised learning, but the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family. The subject is analytical/electrochemical detection of small-molecule pesticides, with ML as an enabling component.

The paper trains an improved YOLOv8n-based object detection network (with ODConv, CBAM and W-IoU modifications) on labelled chest CT data (LUNA16, LIDC-IDRI) for pulmonary nodule detection, a supervised deep learning task. The subject is medical imaging for lung cancer screening, hence the imaging/oncology domain tags.

The paper trains a fully connected neural network (FCNN, i.e. a feedforward MLP built in TensorFlow) from scratch on retrospective DVT patient data to predict postthrombotic syndrome, a supervised tabular prediction task; no depth is claimed, so it is tagged as a classic neural network. The clinical domain is vascular/cardiovascular medicine with an informatics focus on risk prediction modelling.

The paper trains deep learning image classifiers (ResNet34, CNN, Swin Transformer, EfficientNet) in a multi-instance framework, fused with encoded clinical data into a supervised multimodal model for three-class PRISm/COPD stratification. The subject is chest-CT-based detection of a pulmonary function phenotype, hence Medicine/Imaging/Respiratory medicine with Medical imaging at tier 3.

The paper trains a CNN+GNN discriminator (AMP-Hunter) for AMP classification and MIC regression and a generator (AMP-Forge) for sequence synthesis, both from scratch, in a supervised prediction-guided generative loop. Molecular dynamics is a simulation method and the MSA-based selection is a pipeline step, not a tagged model.

The paper develops and internally validates a ridge-penalized logistic regression prediction model for 28-day ICU mortality, a supervised classical ML approach. Restricted cubic splines, bootstrap validation, and decision-curve analysis are statistical evaluation techniques rather than distinct ML models.

The paper trains a LASSO feature-selection step and a multivariable logistic regression prediction model on retrospective clinical data, both classical supervised ML methods, so no pretrained or other model families apply. Domains center on elderly intracerebral hemorrhage patients (neurology/geriatric medicine) with a thrombosis risk prediction model.

The paper trains a Hierarchical Graph Attention Network with graph contrastive learning (self-supervised) for functional connectome fingerprinting, and evaluates it on a downstream supervised psychiatric disorder classification task. The domain is neuroimaging-based individual identification with a psychiatric application.

The paper trains a custom deep learning image-classification network (PGMA-Net) on labelled OSCC histopathology images, so the domains are medicine/oncology/pathology with medical imaging, the paradigm is supervised, and domain adaptation across centers adds a transfer-learning family term alongside deep learning. The abstract names no concrete standard architecture, so the model is tagged verbatim as PGMA-Net.

The paper applies the pretrained AlphaFold 3 model to predict DNA tweezer structures, with no training or fine-tuning reported; HDOCK molecular docking is a simulation method, not an ML model, so it is excluded. Domains reflect computational structural design of DNA nanodevices targeting glioblastoma biomarkers.

The paper trains an original LASSO-Cox prognostic model on sepsis transcriptomic cohorts (supervised) while applying CIBERSORT as-is for immune deconvolution; WGCNA, GSVA, and differential expression are bioinformatics analyses, not ML models, so they are not tagged.

The paper audits LLM-generated physical-activity advice via prompting, output reranking and a comparative panel including DeepSeek, with no training or fine-tuning described. Its subject is algorithmic fairness of AI health guidance in public health, so Medicine/Public health fit best.

This is an external/prospective validation study of a previously developed NLP text-classification system for detecting self-harm in triage notes; the model was not retrained here, so it is applied as-is. No specific algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type stays empty while the NLP family applies.

An oncology nursing study fitting group-based trajectory modelling (a latent-class mixture approach, unsupervised) to identify weight-loss trajectories and training six supervised models, with CatBoost selected as the final interpretable classifier. SHAP is an explainability step and is not tagged as a model type.

The paper trains Bayesian neural networks and feedforward (non-deep) networks on an eight-tissue bioimpedance dataset for supervised classification, and combines base models with a stacking ensemble meta-learner. FRFSM feature generation and temperature scaling are feature-engineering/calibration techniques, not model types, and no deep architecture is named.

The paper trains an AM-CNN-BiLSTM (attention, CNN, and bidirectional LSTM components) on multi-source atmospheric observations to estimate vertical PM2.5, a supervised deep learning task. The fused inputs span lidar aerosol, radiometer thermodynamic profiles, and meteorological data, so multimodal learning also applies; SHAP and ablation are analysis techniques, not model types.

The paper trains tree-based models (RF, XRT, XGBoost, LightGBM) with stacked ensembling on labelled bore data to predict nitrate concentrations, i.e. supervised classical ML/ensemble learning. The subject is environmental modelling of groundwater quality, with machine learning as the applied method.

The paper trains three CNN architectures (ResNet101, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2) from scratch on labelled MRI images for supervised classification of TMJ degenerative joint disease. t-SNE was used for feature-embedding analysis, adding the dimensionality-reduction family, and the domain is medical/dental imaging.

The paper trains an explainable ML classifier (algorithm unnamed) to predict microplastic type and separately fits Gaussian Process regression and unsupervised clustering, giving supervised and unsupervised paradigms with classical machine learning families. SHAP is excluded as an explainability method, and the domain is marine ecological/environmental monitoring.

A vision foundation model is adapted to prostate MRI via patch-level contrastive learning (self-supervised/representation learning) and trained as a weakly supervised (semi-supervised) detection/segmentation model on biopsy-confirmed annotations, so ProViCNet is tagged verbatim with deep learning, representation learning and transfer learning families. Domain centers on prostate cancer MRI detection (Medicine > Oncology, Machine learning > Medical imaging/MRI).

Domains centre on trauma/critical care prediction delivered through a medical-informatics methodology study.

The paper trains five supervised convolutional classifiers (the proposed EDRNet plus VGG16, GoogLeNet, ResNet34 and MobileNetV2) on bare-back images to screen for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. The subject is an AI-based orthopedic screening tool, so the domains map to Medicine, Musculoskeletal medicine, Medical informatics, and Medical imaging.

Domains center on machine learning/computer science applied to agricultural vegetation monitoring, with no applicable tier-3 term.

The paper trains a Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic model on ~39,548 PubMed abstracts to map home health care research themes, an unsupervised natural language processing task within the health services/public health domain. No supervised, deep, or pretrained models are mentioned, so only LDA (classical machine learning, unsupervised, trained in this study) applies.

The paper applies existing spatially aware clustering methods as-is within a benchmarking/consensus framework, training no models itself and naming no specific algorithm or model family; entropy metrics and descriptive spatial statistics are not ML models. The subject domain is spatial transcriptomics method evaluation, captured by Omics/Bioinformatics/Transcriptomics plus Workflows.

The study fits k-means clustering to derive exploratory spinopelvic compensation patterns and trains ridge-regularized logistic regression models (baseline-only and contemporaneous) to predict the composite MCID endpoint. Domain is orthopedic/musculoskeletal clinical research (TKA outcomes) with a strong statistical risk-stratification component.

The paper trains LASSO for variable selection and multivariate logistic regression as the predictive model, both supervised classical ML methods; the nomogram is a visualization of the logistic model and SHAP/RCS are excluded as explanation/statistical analyses. The domain is clinical prediction in drug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis, i.e. medicine/respiratory medicine/infectious disease.

The paper applies over 100 existing VEGA QSAR models as-is and trains auxiliary fingerprint-based models as nonconformity scores, implying supervised training; conformal prediction itself is treated as a calibration framework (excluded from model_type), and no auxiliary model algorithms are named, so no model_family applies. Domains reflect the QSAR/cheminformatics and toxicological endpoint focus with regulatory-scale deployment.

The paper trains decision-tree-based models on paired composition-function data from 558 assembled subcommunities to predict community-level aniline degradation, i.e. a supervised regression task on its own data. The subject is disentangling taxon-specific contributions in a degrading microbial community, fitting Microbiology/Systems biology with a Microbial ecology focus.

The study applies an existing deep learning algorithm (trained on SD-OCT data elsewhere) to fundus photographs without further training, translating its continuous RNFL predictions into diagnostic likelihood ratios for glaucoma. No specific architecture is named, so only the deep learning family applies; domains center on ophthalmic imaging-based diagnostics.

The paper applies two pretrained models as-is (UMA interatomic potential for geometry optimization and ShiftML3 for shielding prediction) without training, so learning_paradigm is empty. Domains reflect NMR crystallography within a computational chemistry workflow; UMA is a well-known deep-learning universal ML interatomic potential, hence deep learning.

rationale: The paper trains a supervised classifier based on discriminant analysis of principal components (DAPC) to distinguish cholangiocarcinoma from PDAC, using PCA (unsupervised dimensionality reduction) feeding a discriminant step, and applies the existing ichorCNA tool as-is to infer tumour fraction and copy-number alterations. Domain is oncology/gastroenterology via bile cfDNA ULP-WGS for malignancy detection and prognosis.

The paper trains multiple machine learning classifiers on classical sequence-derived features and protein language model embeddings to detect AMR proteins, with the pretrained pLM applied as-is to generate embeddings; however, no specific classifier algorithm or architecture is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family remain empty per the evidence rules.

A randomized controlled trial comparing adenoma detection rates using an existing CADe system combined with linked color imaging; no model is trained or fine-tuned and no algorithm or architecture is named, so the CADe tool is tagged verbatim as applied as-is.

This is a data descriptor for a pixel-level annotated longitudinal OCT dataset for macular hole surgery outcomes, placing it in ophthalmic medical imaging. The authors provide a reference nnUNet segmentation baseline trained on their expert-validated pixel-level masks, i.e. a supervised deep learning model, with the resource itself intended to enable future AI modeling.

The paper fits LASSO and SVM-RFE on the GSE69686 expression data to select diagnostic biomarker genes, a supervised classical-ML feature-selection/training task. WGCNA, CIBERSORT, GSEA, docking and the wet-lab validation are pipelines, statistical analyses, or non-ML methods and are therefore not tagged as models.

model_type: ["convolutional neural network", "hidden Markov model", "generative adversarial network"]

The supervised CNN training is the primary learning step, with the HMM and cGAN contributing classical ML and generative deep learning families, respectively.

A clinical prediction model for LVEF recovery after PVC ablation was trained and externally validated on retrospective multicenter data; five ML models were trained, with Random Forest best (AUC 0.88/0.83). Boruta was used only for feature selection, so it is not tagged as a model, and no deep learning or other named architectures are described.

CausalBGM is a Bayesian generative model fitted in this study to learn individual-specific latent (confounder) representations for estimating individual treatment effects, an unsupervised learning of low-dimensional latent features with calibrated posteriors. The application is methodological statistics (causal inference for high-dimensional observational data) with no specific biomedical domain named in the abstract.

The paper trains a deep reinforcement learning navigation policy for wireless capsule endoscopy, benchmarked against vanilla PPO, SAC, and DQN agents, with an adaptive dynamic programming controller for sim-to-real deployment. Domain-wise it targets gastrointestinal diagnostics via endoscopic imaging with a machine-learning method.

The paper trains supervised machine learning models on persistent-homology-derived topological features (BTMs) for protein structure classification, but the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family, so model_type and model_family remain empty. The domain is structural bioinformatics: alignment-free computational classification of protein 3D structures.

The paper trains DyAMNet, a deep attention-based network, end-to-end on labelled EEG identity data (supervised) with a contrastive feature-learning component (self-supervised) and adversarial training for domain-invariant representations. Domains reflect EEG-based biometric identity recognition for brain-computer interfaces in clinical settings.

An XGBoost classifier was trained on multi-center clinical-metabolic biomarkers to differentiate RA from high-inflammatory SjD, a supervised ensemble task. The paper focuses on clinical immunology/rheumatology diagnostics with machine learning as the core method; the transcriptomic analysis is only corroboration, so no tier3 domain term is central.

The paper develops a deep-learning-based digital Single-Molecule Activity Tracker (no specific architecture named, so model_type is left empty) trained to track compartmentalized single-molecule enzyme reactions, implying a supervised training scheme. The subject is single-molecule enzymology in service of long-read sequencing and biotechnological enzyme/motor design.

The paper trains (continued pretraining + LoRA supervised fine-tuning) a Baichuan2-7B-Chat LLM for prostate cancer lifestyle QA, a two-stage self-supervised then supervised learning process. Pretrained LLMs (GPT-3.5-Turbo as comparator; Qwen3-Max and DeepSeek-R1 as prompted referee models) are applied as-is without weight updates, and all models are deep-learning LLMs.

model_type: ["generalized linear model", "random forest", "gradient boosting", "partial least squares"]
rationale: The paper trains classical regression models (GLM, PLS) and tree ensembles (RF, GBM) on acoustic and physical features to predict walnut moisture content, a supervised agricultural/food-science application. Signal-processing steps (WSTD, STFT, VMD) are preprocessing, not model types, and no tier1 or tier3 vocabulary term fits the food-science subject well.

The paper trains a prognostic risk model on TCGA-CESC transcriptomes using L1-regularized (LASSO) Cox regression followed by multivariable Cox regression (supervised), and separately applies NMF clustering for molecular subtyping (unsupervised). Tools like CIBERSORT, TIDE, pRRophetic, and GSEA are analysis pipelines rather than the paper's own trained ML models.

The study applies the pretrained Stable Diffusion model as-is to extract latent representations of paintings and synthesize new artworks, with no training or fine-tuning reported. Its subject is computational analysis of art rather than biomedicine, so domain terms are limited to the machine learning/computer science side.

The paper trains ARIMA, a plain artificial neural network, and a hybrid ARIMA-ANN on historical infant mortality data to forecast future values, a supervised time-series regression task. The subject is public health indicator forecasting in Somalia, with no deeper tier-3 domain applicable.

This is a single-cell RNA-seq study of CNS immune responses to rabies virus; the abstract describes sequencing, cell-atlas construction, and differential expression but names no machine-learning model, algorithm, or pretrained tool, so all modelling fields remain empty per the evidence rules.

The paper trains a TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier and fine-tunes pretrained BERT-based models (BlueBERT, BERT-large) on glioma pathology reports, benchmarked against deterministic RegEx. Domain centers on clinical NLP for molecular marker extraction in neuro-oncology, so Medicine with Medical informatics and NLP, and Molecular medicine at tier 3.

An observational epidemiological study of cardiorenal anemia syndrome (heart failure, chronic kidney disease, anemia) using NHANES/KNHANES survey data, fitting supervised predictive models with LASSO feature selection and 12 internally validated classifiers among which CatBoost performed best; SHAP is an explainability method and the survey-weighted/regression associations are statistical analyses, not predictive models.

The paper records neural activity in monkey area TE and compares it to existing CNN and Vision Transformer models (trained e.g. on ImageNet/stylized ImageNet), applied without further training, so learning_paradigm is empty. The subject is neuroscience of face and surface-quality representations, mapped to Biology/Neurobiology.

The paper applies k-means clustering to identify patient subgroups (unsupervised, trained on its own cohort data). The subject is diabetic retinopathy, spanning ophthalmology and endocrinology/metabolism.

This is a retrospective epidemiological cohort study using multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and performance metrics (AUC, NRI) to test associations, not to train or apply any machine learning model. The domains center on cardiovascular outcomes in oncology survivors.

The task is genomic sequence/feature prediction, placing it in computational biology/bioinformatics with splice sites as nucleic acid sequence features.

The paper analyzes evolutionary constraint (GERP scores), genetic load, and genomic prediction in tetraploid potato breeding material, an omics/genomics study of an agricultural crop. Genomic prediction models were trained on trait phenotypes (supervised), but no specific algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family remain empty per the evidence rules.

The study applies unsupervised k-means clustering to discover CSA phenotypes, then fits adaptive LASSO and multivariable logistic regression within each cluster to identify spasm determinants. It is a clinical cardiology phenotyping study with no deep learning or other model families involved.

A modified ResNet50 with SE/CBAM attention is trained from scratch (supervised classification) on liver MRI images for cirrhosis staging; Grad-CAM is an explainability method and attention modules are components, so the only model type is ResNet within deep learning.

The paper applies the existing pretrained DL_FFLUX machine-learning interatomic potential (a QCT-based MLP) to benchmark simulations of water, ethanol, and small molecules, focusing on parallelization and performance rather than training any model. No new learning occurs in this study, and the abstract names no specific learning architecture beyond the MLP itself.

The study fits latent class analysis (latent profile analysis) on longitudinal TBI cohort data to identify vulnerability profiles, an unsupervised classical ML clustering approach trained in this study. The multivariable logistic regressions are used only to test associations with profile assignment, so they are not listed as model types.

The paper trains NMF on tumor segmentation maps to derive unsupervised spatial components, which are then integrated into Cox proportional hazards models for survival prediction. The domain is clinical neuro-oncology using radiologic tumor imaging data.

The paper trains a supervised symmetry classifier that combines novel persistent GLMY homology topological sequence features with the pretrained ESM2 protein language model in an end-to-end framework. ESM2 is a transformer-based protein language model, so its use implies deep learning with transfer learning; GLMY homology is a topological feature-extraction method rather than a trained model.

An empirical clinical epidemiology study of prediction-model methodology, best captured as Medicine with Statistics and probability; no deeper omics/bioinformatics terms apply. Of the seven compared continuous-predictor modelling approaches (dichotomisation, tertiles, linear/quadratic terms, splines, MFP), only extreme gradient boosting is a named ML model, trained in this study in a supervised fashion.

The paper develops UAV-FlameNet, a modified YOLOv11 object detector trained on the labelled LAWD flame dataset, a supervised deep learning task. The subject is AI-based visual flame detection from UAV imagery, best captured as computer science with imaging and machine learning tiers; no biomedical tier-3 term applies.

The study fits Latent Class Growth Analysis (a latent-class/mixture model) to identify household-chaos trajectories, an unsupervised clustering task, while ANCOVA and ANOVA are statistical association tests and are not tagged as model types. Domains reflect child/adolescent mental health within a pandemic public-health context.

The paper trains linear mixed-effects regression models (with random intercepts) to predict cycloplegic SER from non-cycloplegic binocular ocular parameters, a supervised classical statistical learning approach; SHAP is an explainability method and is excluded. The subject domain is pediatric ophthalmology (refraction/myopia screening) with an ML modeling component.

The paper adapts a pretrained protein language model to experimental fitness rankings via a few-shot 'post-training' algorithm for directed-evolution sequence selection, i.e. fine-tuning with supervised ranking data. The domain is protein engineering/fitness landscape modelling with machine learning, and the model family follows from adapting a large pretrained deep model (transfer/representation learning).

The paper applies an existing, validated LLM to classify decision reasons from free-text verbal reports, with no indication of training or fine-tuning in the abstract, so it is a prompted application of a large language model. The subject domain is the NLP-based analysis of verbal reports, best captured by the NLP tier2 term under a computer science tier1.

The paper benchmarks five off-the-shelf LLMs prompted to extract structured clinical variables from Portuguese medical notes, with no training or fine-tuning of any model. The domain is clinical NLP/data extraction in a medical informatics setting.

The paper trains feedforward multilayer perceptron ANNs (via Levenberg-Marquardt and scaled conjugate gradient) on experimental data to predict CO2 solubility in an ionic liquid, a supervised chemical-property prediction task, so the domain is computational chemistry within chemistry; the plain feedforward MLP is a classic (non-deep) neural network trained in this study.

The paper trains a novel skin-lesion classifier (ZACP) built on EfficientNet with custom attention modules, evaluated on labelled HAM10000 and ISIC2017 datasets, i.e. supervised deep learning. The ZA attention module and Mish activation are model components/training techniques rather than separate model types, so only ZACP and its EfficientNet backbone are listed.

This is an association study using hierarchical block multivariable logistic regression to identify factors linked to admission decisions, explicitly not a predictive tool; per the rules, regression used only to test associations is not tagged as a model type. Domains reflect the hematologic emergency cohort and the retrospective observational clinical study design.

The paper trains a U-Net for coronary segmentation and a multimodal CNN+Transformer fusion model on labelled CTA/radiomics/CT-FFR data to predict high-risk plaques and MACE, i.e. supervised training of deep learning models. Cardiology imaging is the subject domain.

The paper trains a classifier on EEG source-connectivity and microstate features for AD/FTD/control classification, implying supervised training, but the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family, so model_type and model_family are left empty. The subject is EEG-based dementia diagnosis, tagged under Medicine/Neurology with Machine learning as the methods domain.

The paper trains a machine-learning step to prioritise the shared cross-disease gene EGR1 and reports diagnostic AUCs, implying a supervised classifier, but no algorithm or model family is named, so model_type/model_family stay empty. The subject is immunometabolic comorbidity of rheumatoid arthritis and MASLD with transcriptomic biomarker discovery.

The paper trains a Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM) on medical records to flag adults with ASCVD and likely elevated Lp(a), a supervised gradient-boosting ensemble; SHAP is an explainability method and is excluded. The domain is cardiovascular screening enriched via ML applied to health-record data, so Medicine with Cardiology and Medical informatics applies.

A one-dimensional CNN is trained on multimodal clinical data (blood flow, oxygen saturation, intracranial pressure) for supervised prediction of brain temperature, so deep learning and multimodal learning apply. The domain is clinical neuroimaging of acute ischemic stroke, with finite element thermography validated against MRI data.

The authors develop and train hierarchical recurrent deep neural network models with modulatory top-down feedback on an audiovisual integration task, a supervised task-learning setting in computational neuroscience. Domains reflect the modelling of neural computation (Computational biology, Neurobiology) using deep learning (Machine learning); no EDAM tier3 term is specific enough to apply.

The paper evaluates a pre-built deep learning system (DL-VMM) integrated into an analyzer for vaginal smear morphology, with no training or architecture details, so only the 'deep learning' family is taggable and no specific model type is named. Domains reflect the clinical diagnostic application (vaginitis) of an AI microscopy assessment tool.

The paper generates peptide detectability datasets from a single DIA experiment to fine-tune existing detectability prediction models to specific experimental conditions, i.e. transfer learning via supervised fine-tuning on labelled detectability data. No specific model architecture or algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type is left empty.

The paper trains supervised prediction models on labelled speech features to classify MDD and GAD diagnoses, but the abstract only says 'several machine learning models' without naming any algorithm, so model_type and model_family stay empty per the evidence rules. Domain is psychiatry (perinatal depression/anxiety) with machine learning as the applied methodology.

The paper trains a hybrid CNN-Transformer model (CT-TADB) on DNA sequence plus epigenomic tracks (histone marks, CTCF) to predict TAD boundaries, i.e., supervised multimodal deep learning. Cross-cell-type and cross-species performance is evaluated but no pretrained external model is applied or prompted.

The paper trains a gradient boosting model to generate propensity scores for matching in a target trial emulation of nursing home vs home care discharge in older multimorbid patients. The domains reflect geriatric/epidemiological clinical research; the only named ML method is gradient boosting, and the survival analysis is a statistical adjustment, not a listed model type.

The study identifies four identity profiles from self-report questionnaire data, implying an unsupervised person-centred (profile/cluster) analysis trained on the paper's own data, but no specific algorithm, model, or AI tool is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family remain empty. The subject is sport psychology and athlete mental health, best captured by Medicine and Psychiatry.

The paper trains a stacked ensemble species distribution model on occurrence/environmental data (supervised) to predict weed habitat risk, then calibrates predictions against field-derived economic thresholds. No specific base learners are named, so only the stacking/SDM model types and their classical ML + ensemble families are tagged.

The paper develops a colorimetric microfluidic sensing platform for antibiotic detection in food, which is analytical chemistry applied to food safety (agricultural science context). Two supervised models are trained in this study: LDA for classifying antibiotic types/concentrations and an SVM for analyzing real milk samples.

A prognostic model for adjacent segment disease after cervical spine surgery was built using LASSO variable selection and multivariable logistic regression, both classical ML methods trained in a supervised manner on retrospective patient data. The nomogram itself is a presentation of the regression model, not a separate model type.

The paper trains a Cox proportional hazards regression model on clinicopathological data from resected NSCLC patients to derive a prognostic index, stratify risk groups, and predict survival, implemented as standalone software. The subject is lung cancer prognosis prediction (Oncology) with a web-based clinical decision-support tool (Medical informatics).

The paper trains regression models on postural metrics and symptom scores to classify post-concussion visually induced dizziness subtypes (supervised diagnostic classification, AUC reported). No specific algorithm or pretrained model is named beyond regression modelling, and the clinical domain is neurology/vestibular medicine.

The paper fits logistic regression models on DHI records to predict subclinical mastitis risk, validating them on a separate dataset. The multi-factor ANOVA is used for fixed-effect analysis rather than as a predictive model, so only logistic regression is tagged.

The paper is a bioinformatics multi-omics study of OA and T2DM transcriptomic data; its only named ML method/tool is CIBERSORT (an SVR-based pretrained immune-cell deconvolution tool) applied as-is for cell-type estimation. WGCNA, differential expression and pathway analyses are pipeline/network analyses, not model types, and nothing is trained in this study.

The paper trains predictive models on SESI-HRMS breath metabolomics features to estimate serum drug concentrations (supervised regression with k-fold cross-validation), but the abstract names no specific algorithm or model architecture, so model_type and model_family are left empty. Domains reflect clinical pharmacology and metabolomics applied to therapeutic drug monitoring.

The paper trains logistic regression models and uses LASSO with cross-validation for radiomics feature selection to build a predictive nomogram, all supervised classical ML on retrospective ultrasound data. The subject is preoperative prediction in thyroid cancer using ultrasound radiomics, mapping to Medicine/Oncology/Imaging and Medical imaging.

The abstract describes scRNA-seq, intercellular communication analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations but names no specific ML model, algorithm, or trained model; these pipeline/simulation methods are excluded from model_type per the rules. Domains reflect the urological disease focus, the drug-efficacy study, and the transcriptomic methodology.

The paper is an environmental-science study of CO and NO2 patterns using satellite data, with statistical testing and time-series forecasting; no tier1 term matches environmental science, so it is tagged at tier2. The only ML model named is the Prophet time-series model, which is fitted to the paper's own pollutant time series (a supervised regression-style fit) and belongs to the classical machine learning family.

The study is atmospheric/aerosol chemistry (PM2.5 viscosity, N2O5 uptake), fitting best under Chemistry with Environmental science and the analytical poke-and-flow measurement technique; no tier3 vocabulary term matches atmospheric chemistry. The abstract mentions only an unnamed 'machine-learning surrogate' trained to apply the temperature-RH parametrization, so no specific algorithm or family can be tagged, but fitting the surrogate to the derived parametrization implies a trained supervised model.

The paper fits latent class analysis to identify socioeconomic-environmental patterns, an unsupervised classical ML model trained on the study's data; the logistic and mediation regression models are used only to test associations, so they are not tagged as model types. The subject is thyroid disease risk in pregnant women in relation to iodine nutrition and socioeconomic status.

The paper builds machine-learning-based proteomic models and a regulatory network (SWN) to quantitatively predict seed vigor, indicating supervised training on the study's own data, but no specific algorithm or model architecture is named, so model_type and model_family stay empty. The subject is a multi-omics (transcriptomic/proteomic) study of seed vigor regulatory mechanisms in watermelon.

The paper develops an SRS imaging workflow for topical drug permeation (cutaneous pharmacokinetics and bioequivalence), fitting an elastic-net band-selection model on their data (supervised) and unmixing the drug signal with MCR-ALS, an unsupervised matrix-factorization/dimensionality-reduction technique. No pretrained, prompted, or neural models are involved.

domain_tier2: ["Medicines research and development", "Public health and epidemiology"]

The study is a computational reanalysis of public mRNA/miRNA datasets (single-cell and bulk transcriptomics) prioritizing miRNA regulators in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. The only genuine ML model named is LASSO regression, trained on the paper's data in a supervised manner; ROC, PPI, enrichment and database annotations are analyses rather than models.

The paper trains its own Mixture-of-Experts model (MREF-AD) with a gating network for supervised multimodal AD diagnosis from PET/MRI and demographic data, a deep multimodal fusion architecture. The domain is medicine-centred, with medical imaging (MRI/PET) and biomarker use as key tier-3 aspects.

The paper trains an attention-based deep neural network on transcriptomic data for supervised tumor-vs-non-tumor classification, externally tested without refitting. SHAP, Cox models, and pathway analyses are explainability/statistical analyses, not model types, so the only model tagged is the trained attention-based network (deep learning).

The study trains seven task-optimized CNN architectures from scratch (face-identity, object-category, and dual objectives) and compares their representational geometries to MEG recordings, a supervised learning paradigm. The domain is systems/computational neuroscience with millisecond-resolved brain imaging (MEG).

The paper develops and trains a new machine learning model for 3D Sholl analysis of astrocyte morphology, implying supervised training on labelled morphological data, but no algorithm or model family is named, so model_type and model_family stay empty per the evidence rules. The domain is astrocyte/neurobiology research on pathogenic HEPACAM variants causing the rare leukodystrophy MLC.

The paper trains its STRIDE machine-learning sepsis detection models on EHR data across observation windows (supervised), while the label refinement step applies a large language model to discharge summaries via prompting without any stated weight updates. No specific algorithm is named for the core sepsis classifier, so only the LLM is tagged as a model type; the domain centers on ML-based clinical prediction over health records with a label-quality focus.

The paper trains a physics-informed DL motion-correction network exclusively on simulated paired 4DCT data (motion-corrupted inputs with static ground truth), a supervised deep learning setup. The subject is CT imaging methodology in medicine, with machine learning as the enabling technique.
