The abstract applies unspecified 'machine learning' to transcriptomic data to identify PD biomarker genes, so models are trained on the study's own labelled data, but no algorithm, architecture, or model family is named, leaving model_type and model_family empty per the evidence rules. Mendelian randomization, differential expression, docking, and MD simulations are analyses/methods, not ML models.

The paper trains embedding models on multimodal cancer data (with tumor-of-origin/modality recognition tasks implying supervised learning) and evaluates pooled vectors, but names no specific architecture beyond 'embedding models', so representation learning is the only justified family. Domains reflect the computational/AI methodology applied to cancer omics-style data integration.

The paper is a genomic/RNA-sequencing diagnostic study of a rare myopathy; the only AI components are the pretrained splice-prediction tools SpliceAI and SpliceRover applied as-is to validate intronic variant splicing effects, with no training in this study. SpliceAI (and SpliceRover) are well-established deep learning splice predictors.

The paper develops and evaluates four phosphene encoding schemes (rate, sparse, temporal, optim) with a supervised image-classification decoder on simulated prosthetic-vision benchmarks, but the abstract names no concrete ML architecture or algorithm, so model families cannot be assigned from the given evidence. The work is a simulation-based evaluation of visual neuroprosthetic encoding, placing it in computer science/imaging rather than a clinical or omics domain.

The paper develops an approximate expectation-maximization algorithm to jointly estimate particle locations, viewing directions and the 3-D molecular structure directly from cryo-EM micrographs, i.e. an unsupervised maximum-likelihood estimation trained on the paper's own (simulated) data. The domain is computational cryo-EM structure determination, best captured by Structural biology and Electron microscopy.

The paper develops and trains a deep learning framework built on a theoretically guaranteed isometric autoencoder that learns thermodynamic/conformational representations directly from unlabeled cryo-EM data, so training is self-supervised. Domains center on computational analysis of biomacromolecular structure from cryo-EM (ribosome, SARS-CoV-2 spike) data.

The paper presents a framework integrating locally deployed pretrained LLMs with personal knowledge bases and bioinformatics tool invocation, with no training or fine-tuning of models described. HAIant orchestrates LLMs, data, and 84 analytical tools across tasks (records, analysis, manuscript generation), making it an agentic system built on prompted LLMs.

The paper applies unsupervised clustering of allergen-specific IgE sensitization data in dogs, so the learning paradigm is unsupervised and the clustering models are trained on the study's own cohort. However, no specific clustering algorithm or model family is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family are left empty per the evidence rules; the subject is veterinary allergy immunology profiling.

The paper trains ten supervised algorithms on a prospective COVID-19 cohort, explicitly naming random forest, AdaBoost and logistic regression as top performers; SHAP aggregation is an explainability analysis and is not tagged as a model type. The clinical prediction/interpretability focus maps to Medical informatics within Medicine, with the prospective cohort design supporting Public health and epidemiology.

The study trains logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and support vector machine models on retrospective ICU data to predict unfavourable in-hospital outcomes in severe tuberculosis, a supervised task; the models are all non-neural statistical learners, with random forest and XGBoost additionally belonging to ensemble learning. Boruta (feature selection), restricted cubic splines and SHAP are analysis/explainability components rather than the paper's predictive models, and the subject domain is critical-care medicine for an infectious disease.

The paper proposes and trains a new Contrast Stretched Convolutional Neural Network (CSCNN) for supervised classification of tongue tumour sites and grades from histopathology images; the transfer learning CNNs (VGG16, ResNet50, etc.) are only comparator benchmarks and are not listed. The work falls in digital pathology/medical imaging for oncological diagnosis.

The paper trains a quantum-inspired tensor network (Matrix Product State) model from scratch as a supervised classifier on structural MRI features for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder classification, learning distributed feature representations interpreted via graph centrality. No pretrained model is applied, and Shapley values are only an interpretability comparator, not a model.

The paper trains a metabolic classifier on MRS features to predict IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion status, a supervised prediction task in neuro-oncology using magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Since no algorithm or model family is named in the abstract, model_type and model_family are left empty.

The study compares dinucleotide composition across vertebrate and invertebrate genomes, centred on CpG methylation-associated deamination, transposable elements, and evolutionary mutational modelling, fitting genomics/epigenetics and evolutionary domains. The abstract mentions only a generic 'Machine Learning analysis' classifying vertebrates vs invertebrates without naming any algorithm, so model_type and model_family are left empty.

The paper trains a self-supervised machine learning model on bacterial spatial patterns to decode target presence, but names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family remain empty. The subject is inter-kingdom signaling in bacterial collectives responding to Xenopus embryos and Xenobots, best captured as microbiology/systems biology with a microbial ecology aspect.

The paper integrates bulk microarray/RNA-seq and single-nucleus transcriptomics to identify CD53 as a microglia-enriched inflammation marker in spinal cord injury, with machine-learning-based gene prioritization, but no specific algorithm or model family is named, so model_type/model_family stay empty and the ML feature/gene-selection step implies supervised learning. The subject is transcriptomic biomarker discovery in neuroinflammation, hence Omics with Neurobiology and Biomarkers.

The paper trains random forest and logistic regression models on 401 intracerebral hemorrhage patients to predict prognosis after hyperbaric oxygen therapy, a supervised classification task; SHAP is an explainability method and the nomogram a derived output, so only the two trained models are tagged. The subject is clinical neurology (stroke outcomes) with a machine learning methodology component.

The paper develops a compact neural network (encoder-classifier-decoder) whose encoder is pretrained with masked reconstruction (self-supervised) and then fine-tuned with the classifier for beat classification (supervised), with additional federated reconstruction-based adaptation on unlabeled on-device ECG. Cardiology/medical informatics domains fit the arrhythmia-monitoring application, and the privacy-preserving federated design warrants the data security tag.

model_type: ["pyramid neural network", "k-means", "Draco Lizard Optimizer", "Billiards-inspired Ebola Search Optimization Algorithm", "Trimmed Scores Regression"]
rationale: The paper trains a finite-element-informed pyramid neural network classifier for water contamination (supervised), with a k-means-based preprocessing step (unsupervised) and two metaheuristic optimizers used as the paper's own feature selection/extraction methods. Finite-element information is built into the network, matching physics-informed machine learning.

The paper trains a three-input artificial neural network (ANN) on physics-based EMI features plus a statistical index to predict simulated damage states in CFRP composites, a supervised regression/classification task on 105 samples. The hybrid physics-feature/data-driven fusion justifies the physics-informed family, and SHAP is excluded as an explainability method.

The paper fine-tunes the Florence-2 vision-language model on a curated supervised VQA dataset from NLST CT scans and applies a Zephyr-7B LLM in the second stage to generate descriptions and recommendations; GPT-4 is only a comparator baseline, so it is excluded.

The paper trains supervised multimodal models on passive sensor features to detect depression and anxiety, with personalized tree-based models and generic deep learning models; no specific architecture is named beyond 'deep learning'. Domain is psychiatric detection supported by machine-learning methodology.

The study applies an existing Theia3D markerless motion-capture system (a deep-learning-based pose estimation tool) and a Pose2Sim-based pipeline as-is, with no model training, fine-tuning, or prompting reported; agreement metrics (RMSE, MAE, CMC) are statistical analyses, not trained models. The subject is biomechanical movement analysis in athletes, best captured under Medicine with Imaging reflecting the camera-based capture modality.

The paper fits multiple linear regression and ordinal classification models on 65 compounds to predict drug-induced phospholipidosis liability using chromatographic descriptors, so the models are trained here in a supervised paradigm. The subject is QSAR-style modeling of small-molecule safety liabilities in early drug development, best captured by chemistry/cheminformatics with toxicology and medicinal chemistry terms.

The paper is an external evaluation of the commercially implemented AI-CO OCT analysis system, applied as-is with no training or fine-tuning in this study. No architecture or algorithm family for the system is stated in the abstract, so only the tool's verbatim name is tagged; the statistical analyses (Pearson, Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok) are not predictive models.

A physics/engineering study (heat transfer prediction) that trains four supervised regression models — random forest, MLP, XGBoost, and SVR — on a 2,477-sample database of dimensionless flow parameters. No biomedical domain applies, so only Physics and the ML/mathematics tier-2 terms are tagged.

The abstract describes training an explainable machine learning model on retrospective fracture registry data to predict radiographic stability timing, a supervised prediction task in musculoskeletal imaging. No specific algorithm is named (SHAP is an explainability method, not a model), so model_type and model_family remain empty.

model_type: ["Stage-Aware Multimodal Neural Network (SAMNN)", "adversarial synthetic covariate-generation pipeline"]
rationale: The paper trains a deep multimodal neural network (SAMNN) on 13 years of A/H1N1 surveillance data for supervised season-scale influenza forecasting, with an adversarial generative pipeline synthesizing covariates for scenario forecasts. The subject is infectious disease epidemiology (influenza surveillance/forecasting); SHAP is excluded as an explainability method and the five unnamed baselines are comparators.

The paper trains a semi-supervised, genotype-guided hierarchical classifier on Salmonella genomes to predict ecological habitats, with progressive dimensionality reduction of the SNP matrix as an explicit preprocessing/learning step. The abstract names no specific ML algorithm, but the 'node-associated decision-making models' structured as a hierarchy of splitting rules correspond to decision trees; Panaroo is a pangenome analysis pipeline, not a trained model.

The paper trains a deep anomaly-detection model and a severity estimator on two labelled healthcare IoT attack datasets (supervised), while a reinforcement-learning component selects trusted rollback checkpoints via a Q-Score. No specific deep architecture is named, so only the generic deep neural network and the verbatim reinforcement learning framework are tagged.

The paper develops RAR, a semi-supervised medical image segmentation framework trained in this study that uses retrieval and contrastive (self-supervised) learning to enrich representations of unlabeled data; no concrete architecture beyond the framework itself is named. It explicitly does not fuse multimodal features, so multimodal learning is excluded.

The paper develops an unsupervised denoising framework built on pairwise TCR similarity (TCRbase/TCRdist3) with hierarchical clustering and a modified silhouette score, and retrains NetTCR (supervised) on the denoised data, while AlphaFold 3 is applied as-is for structural validation. Domains center on computational immunology/bioinformatics with a data-quality focus.

The paper develops a Raman-spectroscopy-based soft sensing model trained on its own fermentation data to predict pigment formation, implying supervised training, but the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family. The subject is industrial fungal fermentation process control, best captured by Biology/Biotechnology.

The paper trains tensor-train-compressed physics-informed neural networks from scratch on PDE benchmark problems (Burgers, Black-Scholes), fitting the PDE residual and boundary/initial conditions. The domains are computational/applied-mathematics machine learning for PDE solving rather than any biomedical application, so no tier3 biomedical terms apply.

The paper develops an all-atom neural network potential embedded in a coarse-grained MM environment, with the NNP-CG coupling terms fitted via supervised force-matching (MS-CG) on reference data. The domain is computational chemistry/molecular simulation, with molecular dynamics and molecular modelling as the concrete tier-3 topics.

The paper trains CNN, BiLSTM and Transformer regressors on labelled RBS strength data (supervised) and a WGAN-GP generative model to synthesize new RBS sequences (unsupervised generative learning), all trained in this study. Domain is synthetic biology / biotechnology sequence design, supported by transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of RBS activity.
